seoDescription: Custom indoor stickers on paper, vinyl or BOPP for walls, shelves, doors, packaging and displays. Removable adhesive for painted walls, any shape, free proof.
tagline: Paper, vinyl or BOPP stickers for walls, shelves, doors, counters and packaging that never see weather.
quickAnswer: Indoor stickers are printed on matte or gloss paper, vinyl or BOPP film for surfaces that stay out of sun and rain: walls, shelves, doors, counters, packaging and displays. They skip the laminate an outdoor sticker needs, so they cost less and come with removable adhesive for painted walls. sections.h2: Walls, shelves, doors and packaging: where indoor stickers belong
sections.html:
Most stickers never go outside. They go on a stockroom shelf, a cafe wall, an office door, a product box or a trade show counter, and for those jobs an outdoor build is money spent on sun protection the sticker will never need. An indoor sticker uses a lighter film or a paper stock, a thinner finish and, where the surface is painted, a removable adhesive that comes off without taking the paint with it. The print is the same full-color CMYK with Pantone matching, and the shapes are the same: die cut to your outline, kiss cut on sheets, or wound on rolls.

The nearest sibling is our outdoor sticker, which stacks a thicker outdoor vinyl, a UV laminate and a permanent adhesive to survive years of weather. If the sticker will sit in a sunny window, on a vehicle or on anything that gets rained on, the custom outdoor sticker page is the right product. For everything under a roof, this one is cheaper and easier to remove.

sections.h2: Paper, vinyl or BOPP for an interior job
sections.html:
Indoor use does not mean one material. A wall quote in a yoga studio, a price label on a shelf edge and a logo seal on a bakery box each want a different stock. Here is how we match them.

Paper is the budget choice and takes a pen, so it suits anything hand-dated or hand-numbered. Vinyl wipes clean and survives a mop bucket splashing a baseboard. BOPP sits between the two for products that get handled with wet hands. The full list of stocks, including holographic and metallic films for retail displays, is on our sticker materials category.

sections.h2: Wall and shelf labels that come off clean
sections.html:
The question we get most about interior stickers is not how well they stick but how well they let go. Lease walls, painted lockers and laminate shelving all need a sticker that peels in one piece a year later. Removable acrylic adhesive on vinyl does that on these surfaces:

  • Painted drywall with eggshell, satin or semi-gloss paint, cured at least two weeks. Flat and matte paints hold less and may flake.
  • Laminate and melamine shelving in stockrooms and retail bays, including shelf-edge strips up to 36 inches long.
  • Glass doors and partitions, where clear vinyl gives a frosted-look privacy band or a logo with no white edge.
  • Painted steel lockers, filing cabinets and doors, once wiped with alcohol.
  • Stainless and plastic bins for kitchens and labs, with vinyl or BOPP rather than paper.
  • Whiteboards and acrylic signs, where a removable sticker can be swapped each quarter.

Permanent adhesive is still the better pick for product packaging and anything that must not be peeled off by a customer. For stickers that go on and off many times, the static cling and restickable builds on our custom reusable sticker range are the right construction.

sections.h2: Choosing an indoor sticker in five decisions
sections.html:
Work through these in order and the quote will be right the first time.

  1. Surface: painted wall, glass, laminate, cardboard or plastic. This decides the adhesive, removable for paint and glass, permanent for packaging.
  2. Handling: will it be touched, wiped or splashed? Vinyl or BOPP if yes, paper if it sits untouched on a box or wall.
  3. Size: measure the space in inches and allow a margin. Shelf-edge labels run 1 to 2 inches tall; wall graphics go up to 24 by 36 inches in one piece.
  4. Shape: a circle or rectangle is the cheapest cut; a die cut to your logo outline costs a little more and reads better on a wall.
  5. Finish: matte under bright lighting, gloss for packaging and color-heavy art, spot UV where you want a logo to catch the light on a flat matte label.

Send us the answers with a vector file or a 300 dpi image and the free proof comes back with the cut line and adhesive noted.

sections.h2: Finish choices under store and office lighting
sections.html: Indoor light is the thing outdoor buyers never think about and indoor buyers get wrong. Overhead fluorescent tubes and LED spots bounce off a gloss sticker at eye level, so a glossy wall graphic in a hallway or a shelf label under a spotlight can be hard to read from a few feet away. Matte kills that glare and photographs better for product listings. Gloss earns its place on packaging, on small stickers held in the hand, and on artwork with deep blacks and saturated color, where the shine adds depth that matte flattens out. Spot UV gives the best of both: a matte sticker with a gloss logo or pattern raised over it, which works well on cosmetics and gift packaging. If the choice is still not obvious, our matte versus glossy finish guide shows both under the same light.

Prices start at $0.30 per sticker and move with size, quantity and material; paper is the least expensive, vinyl and BOPP a little more. The minimum is 100 stickers per design, and several designs can share one order. We send a free digital proof before anything prints and fix artwork at no charge. Production takes 5 to 7 business days after approval, delivery lands inside 8 to 10 business days, and FedEx shipping within the United States is free. Rush production is available if you give us the date.

Sheets and singles ship flat; rolls come on a 3 inch core. Store spare stickers flat, out of sunlight and away from a heater, and the adhesive stays good for a year or more. Defective stickers are reprinted at no charge within the 10 day return window. The rest of our products, including the formats that bridge indoor and outdoor use, are listed on the Die Cut Stickers home page.

faqs.q: What are indoor stickers made of?
faqs.a: Paper, vinyl or BOPP film, chosen by the surface and how much handling the sticker gets. Paper is the cheapest and takes a pen, vinyl wipes clean and flexes around corners, and BOPP resists moisture on cosmetics and food jars. None of them carry the thick UV laminate an outdoor sticker needs, which keeps the price down.

faqs.q: Will indoor stickers pull paint off a wall when I remove them?
faqs.a: Not with removable adhesive on cured eggshell, satin or semi-gloss paint. Peel slowly at a low angle and the sticker comes off in one piece with no residue. Flat and matte paints bond weakly to the wall itself and can flake with any sticker, so test one in a hidden spot or mount the graphic on a panel.

faqs.q: Can indoor stickers go on shelves and bins in a stockroom?
faqs.a: Yes. Laminate and melamine shelving take removable vinyl well, and shelf-edge strips can run up to 36 inches long in one piece. For plastic bins and stainless shelving that get wiped or splashed, order vinyl or BOPP rather than paper, with permanent adhesive if the label must stay through cleaning.

faqs.q: Do indoor stickers need a laminate?
faqs.a: Usually not. Out of sunlight the ink keeps its color for years without one, which is a large part of why indoor stickers cost less. Add a gloss or matte laminate only if the sticker will be scrubbed, handled constantly or placed where cleaning chemicals reach it, such as a kitchen counter or a lab bench.

faqs.q: Are paper indoor stickers strong enough for a retail counter?
faqs.a: On the front face of a counter, where fingers and cleaning cloths pass over it every day, paper scuffs within weeks. Use white vinyl there. Paper is fine on the box, the bag, the shelf tag and the wall behind the counter, where nothing touches it once it is on.

faqs.q: Can interior stickers go on a bathroom wall or near a sink?
faqs.a: Yes, if they are vinyl or BOPP rather than paper. Steam and splashes do not harm either film, and the inks are sealed on the surface. Apply to tile, painted drywall or a mirror once the surface is dry, press the edges firmly and give the adhesive a day before the room is used.

faqs.q: What happens if I use indoor stickers outside?
faqs.a: Paper swells and tears in the first rain, and unlaminated vinyl begins to fade within a season in direct sun, with the adhesive softening on a hot surface. A covered porch or a shaded entryway is usually fine for vinyl. For anything in sun or weather, the outdoor build with laminate is worth the difference.

faqs.q: Which indoor sticker finish reads best under store lighting?
faqs.a: Matte. Fluorescent tubes and LED spots reflect off gloss at eye level, so a glossy wall or shelf sticker shows a bright hot spot that hides the text from certain angles. Keep gloss for packaging and small hand-held stickers, and use spot UV when you want a shiny logo on a matte background.

faqs.q: How big can an indoor wall sticker be?
faqs.a: Up to 24 by 36 inches in one piece. Larger murals are printed as tiled panels with a half-inch overlap marked on the proof. Removable vinyl is the right stock for a wall at that size, applied from the top edge down with a squeegee so air escapes ahead of the film.

faqs.q: Do indoor stickers work on glass doors and office partitions?
faqs.a: Yes. Clear vinyl lets the glass show through around the artwork, with a white ink layer printed behind light colors so they stay visible. A frosted-effect band at eye height is the common request for partitions and conference rooms. Removable adhesive peels off glass cleanly when the layout changes.

faqs.q: How many indoor stickers do I have to order?
faqs.a: 100 stickers per design is the minimum, from $0.30 each depending on size, quantity and the stock: paper, vinyl or BOPP. Several designs can share one order, so a set of shelf labels or room signs with different text can reach the minimum together rather than 100 of each.

faqs.q: How long will indoor stickers keep their color?
faqs.a: Out of direct sunlight, vinyl and BOPP hold their color for 3 to 5 years and paper for 1 to 2 years before any visible change. A sticker inside a sunny window is the exception, since glass does not block the UV that fades ink; order the laminated outdoor build for that spot.
